newsitem.title: BELARUS: Top Belarus prosecutor resigns, health blamed.
newsitem.headline: Top Belarus prosecutor resigns, health blamed.

text.p: Hardline Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko on Thursday accepted the resignation of the country's top prosecutor, the latest in a string of officials to quit.
An aide to General Prosecutor Vasily Kapitan told Reuters that Lukashenko had accepted Kapitan's resignation "for health reasons".

Kapitan went to hospital with a heart problem after a controversial referendum on November 24 in which Lukashenko won an overwhelming mandate for sweeping powers over the former Soviet republic's institutions.
Lukashenko appointed Oleg Bozhelko, 41, a prosecutor from his home region of Mogilyov, to replace Kapitan.
Some analysts say Kapitan was not loyal to Lukashenko and that he had launched criminal proceedings against the presidential guard after it threw electoral chief Viktor Gonchar out of office.
Lukashenko sacked Gonchar, even though he was appointed by parliament, days before the referendum. Gonchar had said he would not recognise the vote.
The president also signed a decree on Thursday appointing Ivan Lyakh as Labour Minister to replace Alexander Sosnov who resigned last month with then Prime Minister Mikhail Chigir.
Lukashenko has been attacked by Western governments and organisations over the referendum, which they say was not completely free or fair.
Several top Belarus officials -- including the prime minister -- have resigned in the political turmoil provoked by the referendum in the usually peaceful country of 10 million people.
The Constitutional Court also opposed Lukashenko by ruling that a series of his decrees were illegal. Seven of its 11 judges, including its head, have resigned in protest.
